in case of any danger. Weche walked to the gate. Weche and his grandfather were shocked to find
the gate open. Could the animals have broken loose? Weche wondered. He then walked fast
towards the cowshed. To his relief, all the animals were there peacefully chewing cud. But still
he heard some noise behind the store. He walked there and what he saw shocked him. He came
face to face with, the bull his father had sold in the market two days ago.

Soma kifungu kifuatacho kisha ujibu swali la 1 hadi la 6.
Watu wengi hushangaa jinsi ulimwengu unavyobadilika kwa mwendo wa kasi. Maendeleo
yanazidi kushuhudiwa katika sekta za kiuchumi, kisiasa na kijamii. Hata hivyo, ni dhahiri kuwa
maendeleo haya yameiletea jamii manufaa na madhara.
Sekta ya kijamii imekumbwa na mabadiliko si haba. Hapo awali, jamii nyingi ziliienzi na
kuikumbatia mienendo ifaayo. Mtoto aliyeonyesha dalili za kupotoka, kwa mfano, alikashifiwa vikali sio
tu na wazazi au walezi wake bali na jamii nzima. Mtoto alikuwa mali ya jamii. Kwa sababu hiyo, jamii
ilimwelekeza ilivyostahili ikifahamu kuwa, mtoto umleavyo ndivyo akuavyo. Katu jamii haikumdekeza
mtoto, bali ilimrudi aliyekosa papo hapo.
Inasikitisha kuona jinsi ambavyo mambo yamebadilika kwa upande wa mavazi. Yamekuwa
mazoea kwa baadhi ya waja kuvalia mavazi yanayowaacha nusu uchi! Isitoshe, wengine wao hujipiga
picha na kuzisambaza kwenye mitandao bila soni. La ajabu ni kwamba, wanaofanya hivyo ni wakubwa
kwa wadogo, wake kwa waume.
Kwa upande mwingine, baadhi ya vijana huwavunjia heshima wakubwa wao. Utawapata katika
matwana wameziba masikio yao kwa vidude hata wanapoombwa kiti na mzee hawasikii. Nayo lugha
wanayoitumia kuwasiliana na wazee hawa imekosa adabu. Sikwambii vituko wanavyovifanya hadharani.
Ajabu! Wanaenda kinyume cha mila na desturi za jamii zao na kusahau kuwa mwacha mila ni mtumwa.
Ukweli ni kwamba, uadilifu ni muhimu kwa mtu yeyote. Maadili hayafai kupuuzwa eti kwa
sababu ya maendeleo. Watu wote wanafaa kuwa na mienendo inayokubalika katika jamii. Maendeleo
yawe njia ya kuendeleza jamii bali si ya kuididimiza.
1. Kulingana na kifungu, ni kweli kuwa:

B.      Mabadiliko ulimwenguni hupendwa na watu wengi.

B.      Mtoto aliyefanya makosa alishtakiwa na wazazi na walezi.

C.     Mitandao inawavutia watu ambao hawana haya.
D.     Jamii hushangazwa na mitindo mbalimbali ya mavazi.
4. Bainisha jinsi vijana wanavyokosa nidhamu kulingana na aya ya nne.
A.     Husikiliza muziki wanaposafiri.
B.     Wanawadharau wazee.
C.     Wanatumia lugha isiyoeleweka.
D.     Hupuuza jamii.
5. Mambo yafuatayo yanaweza kutendeka jamii ikisahau utamaduni wake isipokuwa:
A.     Uhusiano kati ya vijana na wazee utazorota.
B.     Amani itakosekana katika jamii.
C.     Wanajamii watakuwa kama wafungwa.
D.     Vijana wengi watajiendeleza kiuchumi.
6. Neno, haikumdekeza limetumiwa katika kifungu. Chagua kisawe cha neno hilo.
A.     haikumridhisha
B.     haikumhimiza
C.     haikumbembeleza
D.     haikumfurahisha
Geuza ukurasa
Soma kifungu kifuatacho kisha ujibu swali la 7 hadi la 12.
Zamani, Paka na Panya walikuwa marafiki wa kufa kuzikana. Waliishi pamoja na kufanya
shughuli nyingi kwa ushirikiano. Waliwinda, wakapika, wakaosha vyombo na hata kufua nguo zao
pamoja. Wakati mwingine, walifanya kazi zao kwa zamu.
Siku moja, Paka na Panya walipata mwaliko wa kuhudhuria harusi kati ya Beberu na
Mtamba. Walifurahi kama kibogoyo aliyeota meno. Kila mmoja wao aliuona mwaliko huo kuwa fursa
nzuri ya kujifurahisha. Panya alitamani kula vyakula vitamu harusini.
Paka naye, alipanga kuonyesha madaha yake. Kawaida yake, Paka alijivunia ngozi yake ya
kupendeza yenye madoadoa meupe na meusi. Wote wawili walianza kujiandaa kwa minajili ya siku hiyo
adimu na muhimu. Walijishonea nguo za vitenge zilizopendeza mno.
Kabla ya siku ya sherehe, Paka na Panya walivaa marinda yao ili kuhakikisha yalikuwa sawa.
Panya alimwangalia Paka akagundua kuwa rinda lake lilikuwa maridadi zaidi. Alimwonea gere. Usiku
huo, Panya aliamka usiku wa manane na kunyatanyata hadi lilipokuwa rinda la Paka. Aliliumauma
likararuka raruraru kisha akarudi kulala.
Siku ya siku ilipofika, Paka na Panya waliamka alfajiri mbichi kujitayarisha. Walioga kisha
wakaelekea kuvaa marinda yao. Salaale! Rinda la Paka lilikuwa tambara lisilotamanika. Paka hakuamini
macho yake. Machozi yalimtiririka njia mbilimbili. Panya alijifanya kumhurumia Paka. Hata hivyo,
Paka alijua kuwa tendo hilo la kinyama halikufanywa na mwingine ila Panya. Paka alipandwa na mori
akataka kumvamia Panya. Panya alipoona hayo, alimwomba mwenzake amsamehe. Paka alimsamehe
lakini moyoni alijiambia kuwa, kweli kikulacho ki nguoni mwako. Tangu siku hiyo, urafiki wa Paka na
Panya uliingia doa.

Miaka ya nyuma, jamii nyingi humu nchini zilijivunia kuwa na watu waliomiliki nguvu za kiajabuajabu.
Watu hawa waliokuwa na nguvu zisizo za kawaida, waliogopwa na kuheshimiwa. Walichukuliwa kama
kitambulisho cha jamii zao.
Katika jamii ya Akamba, hadithi husimuliwa kumhusu nabii wa kike aliyeitwa Syokimau.
Syokimau aliishi katika karne ya kumi na tisa kwenye milima ya Iveti, karibu na mji wa Machakos.
Inasemekana kuwa, licha ya kuwa nabii, Syokimau alikuwa mganga mahiri. Alikuwa na uwezo wa kutabiri
matukio ya baadaaye na kutibu magonjwa mbalimbali.
Ubashiri wa Syokimau uligonga ndipo; kila alichotabiri kilitukia. Alitabiri kuhusu uvamizi kutoka
kwa jamii jirani mathalan Agikuyu na Maasai. Uvamizi huo ulipotokea uliwapata wapiganaji wa jamii yake
wakiwa wamejiandaa. Aliona joka refu lililokuwa likitema moto pamoja na moshi. Joka hilo liliwashusha
watu waliokuwa na ngozi iliyofanana na nyama. Haya yalitimia wakati ambapo wazungu walikuja na
kujenga mtambo wa reli. Syokimau alibashiri kuhusu kuzuka kwa kizazi cha kushangaza ambacho
kingevunja miiko. Kizazi cha sasa kina mitindo isiyoeleweka katika mavazi yao na lugha wanayotumia.
Syokimau aliagua ndwele mbalimbali zilizowasumbua watu wa jamii yake. Baadhi ya ndwele
hizo zilishukiwa kuwa za kishirikina. Kipawa hiki kilimfanya Syokimau kuheshimiwa na watu wa jamii
yake.
Kifo cha Syokimau ni kitendawili. Kuna madai kuwa alifariki na kufufuka mara mbili kabla ya
kuaga dunia kabisa mara ya tatu. Inaaminika kuwa eneo la sasa la Syokimau limepewa jina hilo kutokana
na shujaa huyo. Hali kadhalika, mnara umejengwa kwa heshima yake katika kituo cha Reli cha Syokimau.

2.   Soma hadithi ifuatayo kisha ujibu maswali.
Hapo zamani za kale Simba na Swara walikuwa marafiki wa chanda na pete.
Walitembea pamoja, walilima pamoja, waliwinda pamoja na hata kula pamoja.
Watoto wa Simba na Swara nao waliiga tabia za wazazi wao. Unajua tena mwana
akibebwa hutazama kisogo cha nina. Wana hawa walikuwa mkono wazi kwa wenzao.
Waliwakirimia mengi, si wanasesere wa kuchezea, si mipira ya kabumbu waliotengeneza
wenyewe kwa vitambaa vikuukuu…kila kitu kizuri walichoambulia kiliwafaa wote. Ile
kauli ya mkulima ni mmoja walaji ni wengi ikatimia.
Siku moja, Simba na Swara waliamua kwenda mawindoni.
“Walete wanao kwangu ili wacheze pamoja wakitusubiri tuwaletee vitoweo.” Swara
alimwambia Simba. Simba alikubali kwani alimwamini sana rafikiye Swara.
Walifululiza hadi kichakani kuwinda kama ilivyokuwa kawaida yao. Ghafla, Simba
akajisingizia kukumbwa na jambo fulani. Alimwomba Swara aendelee kuwinda, yeye
akimbie nyumbani kidogo. Swara alikubali mara moja. Simba alitimua mbio. Punde si
punde alifika kwa Swara na kuwapata watoto wote wamelala. Simba aliwaamsha watoto
wa Swara na kuwabembeleza kumfuata. Aliwapeleka kwenye boma lake la siri na
kuwaficha huko. Aliwapa kila aina ya vitafunio nao wakafurahia sana. Simba alikuwa na
mpango wa kuwala wana wa Swara mmoja mmoja hadi waishe.
Swara alipatwa na wasiwasi alipomwona mwenzake amekawia kurudi. Alitoka
shoti na kurudi nyumbani kwake. Alipata Simba akipiga unyende huku amejishika kichwa
hivi.
“Kuna nini mwenzangu?” Swara aliuliza. “Jamani hawa watoto wameingia kwenye
shimo gani? Kweli mzee Fisi anaweza kuwa amewageuza kitoweo?” Alijisemea Simba
bila kumwangalia Swara. Wakati wote huu Swara alikuwa anamtazama Simba kana
kwamba hajamwambia lolote la kushughulisha. Swara alivuta fikra akaanza kumshuku
Simba. Akajiuliza, “Kwa nini Simba aliniacha kichakani na kurudi nyumbani wakati ule?”
Alianza kumfuata Simba kisiri kila mara.
Siku moja, Swara alibaki kinywa wazi alipomwona Simba akiingia katika boma
lake la siri. Aliwaona watoto wao wote wakicheza kwa furaha. Hakuweza kujificha tena.
Alijitokeza kwa hasira akawachukua wanawe na kurudi nao nyumbani. Simba aliona haya
akashindwa kumwangalia kwa macho rafiki yake. Uzuri ni kuwa hakuwa ameanza
kutekeleza unyama wake. Tangu siku hiyo, Simba na Swara wakawa maadui wakubwa.
Hadithi yangu inaishia hapo.

Jina la Fatuma, mwanawe Bwana Makali lilikuwa na sifa si haba katika kijiji cha
Mandongo kama walivyokiita wengi. Nafikiri sifa zake zilitokana na weledi wake
masomoni. Ama tuseme alikuwa wembe masomoni. Fatuma alikuwa na ndoto ya kuwa
mhandisi. Ndoto hii ilimsukuma kufanya kila jitihada masomoni. Alinuia kuikwamua aila
yake kutoka kwenye lindi la ukata.
Shuleni, mwalimu mkuu na hata walimu wengine walimsifu Fatuma. Nidhamu
pamoja na bidii yake ilikuwa ya kupigiwa mfano. Wanafunzi wenzake walimchagua kuwa
kiranja mkuu wa shule. Halima, mama yake Fatuma alijikakamua kufanya kazi ya kijungu
jiko ili kukidhi mahitaji ya Fatuma shuleni. Wengi walimfahamu kama Mamafua pale
Mandongo. Wakati mwingine, Mamafua angeshiriki hata shughuli za ujenzi kusudi
mwanawe asikose cha kutia tumboni. Hakika Mamafua alikuwa mwenye bidii ya mchwa.
Fatuma naye alizidi kutia bidii masomoni.
Wakati haya yote yakitukia, Makali, babake Fatuma alikuwa amehamia katika kijiji
cha Changale. Waulize wenzake nao watakwambia kugura kwake kulichochewa na
utamaduni au tuseme mahitaji ya utamaduni wenyewe kwake. Mja huyu alishindwa kabisa
kustahimili vijembe kwa kutoipa jamii yake mvulana wa kurithi mila za jamii yao. Fatuma
naye alizidi kutia bidii masomoni. Hatimaye aliibuka mwanafunzi bora katika tathmini ya

Habari za ufanisi wa Fatuma masomoni zilisambazwa kwenye mitandao ya kijamii. Hata
Makali alizipata habari hizo kutoka huko alikokuwa. Machozi ya furaha yalimtiririka.

Onyesho 1

ya kufunga shule. Kaima ni mwanafunzi wa Gredi ya 7. Begani amebeba mkoba wenye

17. Your class is planning to start an enterprise project in the school. The first activity the class should

SECTION A (20 marks)
Answer ALL the questions in this section.
1.   Social Studies is an important subject that makes a learner into an effective citizen. Which one of
the following is another reason for studying the subject?
A.      To enable the learners to conduct experiments.
B.     To enable the learners to develop critical thinking skills.
C.     To enable the learners to understand their religion.
D.     To enable the learners to know the laws of nature.
2.   Gender stereotyping is a case of somebody treating people of the opposite sex negatively.
This problem can be solved by different ways. Which one of the following is the least
effective way of dealing with this problem?
A.     Providing equal opportunities to both males and females.
B.     Providing more opportunities to women.
C.     Basing roles of males and females on the traditional beliefs.
D.     Allowing men to dominate in leadership.
3.   Elements of weather are measured using different instruments. Which element is measured
using the instrument shown below
A.     Rainfall.
B.     Wind speed.
C.     Wind direction.
D.     Sunshine.
4.   At 10:00 a.m., Fatuma, who is at Kisumu, on longitude 32° E calls her friend Halima,
who is at Dar es Salaam, on longitude 39° E. What time will it be at Dar es Salaam?
A.     9: 32. am
B.     8: 10 am
C.     10:28 am.
D.     9: 23 am.
3                                        Turn Over
5.   The existence of many archaeological sites in Africa is one of the pieces of evidence that
humankind originated from Africa. Which other factor supports this evidence?
A.     Nearness to the sea.
B.     Presence of savannah grasslands.
C.     Its strategic location in the world.
D.     Existence of hills and mountains.
6.   Evolution is one of the theories that explain the origin of human beings. Give the name of the
scientist who came up with this theory.
A.     Dr. Louis Leakey.
B.     Michael Faraday.
C.     Isaac Newton.
D.     Sir Charles Darwin.
7.   Personal peace is the calmness that comes as a result of an understanding of oneself. One of
the ways of promoting this peace is
A.     Sharing information about others.
B.     Sharing with people we trust.
C.     Solving people’s problems.
D.     Promoting the welfare of others.
8.   Grade 7 learners carried out library research on the economic activities of the Zulu and the
Ogiek up to 1900. Give a common economic activity practised by the two communities.
A.     Beekeeping.
B.     Pottery making.
C.     Hunting.
D.     Iron smelting
9.   Africa was colonised by the European powers in the 19th century. From the table shown, select
the colonial power that is correctly matched with its colony.
Country              Colony
A    Britain              Kenya
B    Belgium              Namibia
C    Spain                Angola
D    France               Congo
10.   To boost self-esteem, one needs to develop confidence in themselves. What else can one do to
promote self-esteem?
A.     To constantly compare oneself with others.
B.     To set goals and work towards achieving them.
C.     To carefully keep the memory of past failures.
D.     To analyse shortcomings and blame others.
11.   Grade 8 learners used digital devices to research on the forms of slavery and servitude. From
the options below, choose the type of slavery where a person is regarded as owner’s property.
A.     Military slavery.
B.     Chattel slavery.
C.     Domestic slavery.
D.     Debt slavery.
12.   Favourable climate led to the growing of several crops in the ancient kingdom of Kongo.
Which of the following crops was grown in the kingdom?
A.     Maize.
B.     Tea.
C.     Cotton.
D.     Millet.
13.   Money was first used as a medium of exchange in the 19th century. Which of the following
features of money made it a good medium of exchange?
A.     Durability and divisibility.
B.     Transaction of goods and services.
C.     Uniformity across nations
D.     Ready availability.
14.   Healthy relationships are necessary for peaceful coexistence in a school environment with
different cultures. Which of the following skills hinder healthy relationships?
A.     Negotiation and problem-solving skills.
B.     Creativity and imagination skills.
C.     Effective communication and assertiveness skills.
D.     Collaboration and critical thinking skills.
5                                        Turn Over
15.   A resource person discussed with Grade 8 learners the situations that may lead to conflicts in
the family. Select a situation that may not cause family conflicts from the options provided.
A.     Economic hardships.
B.     Alcohol abuse.
C.     Influence of role models.
D.     Divorce of parents.
16.   Different types of maps represent part, or the whole earth on a flat surface. These maps are used
in the learning of Social Studies. Which of the following types is least used in Social Studies?
A.     Sketch.
B.     Atlas.
C.     Google.
D.     Topographical.
17.   Grade 8 learners conducted a field study on factors that influence human activities in the school
neighbourhood. Give the most suitable method of data collection that they used.
A.     Questionnaire.
B.     Counting.
C.     Tabulation
D.     Photographing.
18.   Keith, a Kenyan who lives in Australia with his family has recently acquired Australian
citizenship. Which type of citizenship does he possess?
A.     Citizenship by birth.
B.     Citizenship by adoption.
C.     Dual citizenship.
D.     Citizenship by registration.

B.     Loss of life.
C.     Loss of employment.

B.     Improved health services.

THE KENYA NATIONAL EXAMINATIONS COUNCIL
KENYA JUNIOR SCHOOL EDUCATION ASSESSMENT
KJSEA
911/1
CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS (Project)
Paper 1
SAMPLE PAPER
JANUARY 2025
DURATION: 3 months
INSTRUCTIONS TO SCHOOLS
1.   This is a project paper which should be taken in 3 months, during Term II (May to
August).
2.   Teachers are provided with scoring guides.
3.   The project will be assessed in phases, where each milestone should be scored,
and a record maintained for each learner.
This document consists of 4 printed pages.
1                                    Turn over
©2025 The Kenya National Examinations Council
1. INTRODUCTION
(i)   This is an integrated project assessment comprising activities from all component
disciplines in the Creative Arts and Sports subject (Visual Arts, Performing Arts and
Sports).
(ii)  With the guidance of the teacher, learners are required to fully undertake this project,
whose assessment scores will form part of the final summative assessment of the learner
in this subject.
(iii) Each Task will be assessed using a given assessment rubric. Learners should be allowed
to access the assessment rubric in order to fully align their activities to the requirements
of the task.
2. PROJECT DESCRIPTION
A Creative Arts and Sports Festival is an opportunity for learners to showcase their talents and
celebrate creativity, athleticism, and cultural heritage. Your school is to host the annual Creative
Arts and Sports Festival. The event will include an art exhibition, folk song performances, sports
competitions, and storytelling sessions.
You are required to carry out the following four tasks in preparation for the event:
Task 1: Visual Arts
Design a multimedia poster measuring 30 cm × 42 cm for the upcoming event themed “Artistry in
Motion”. The event will be held on a selected day at the school playground.
Individually,
(i) conduct research then make notes and produce sketches to conceptualise the idea, (these
should be placed in the assessment portfolio)
(ii) create letter forms and illustrations using variety of paper, fabric and any other suitable
found materials. (Computer application may also be used for creating the letter forms). The
poster should incorporate the following.
(a)     theme
(b)     date, time, venue
(c)     suitable colour scheme, illustrations, images and legible lettering
(d)     organised layout with a clear and brief message
The completed poster should be neat and appropriately finished.
Set up an exhibition for the created posters to be viewed by the attendees on the day of the
festival.
Task 2: Music and Dance
You are required to:
a) Select a folksong from a Kenyan community for a performance lasting 2 – 3 minutes.
b) Train the folksong to a group of 8 – 12 members. Pay attention to the following aspects:
(i) Authenticity singing with clear diction, vocal blend, and projection.
(ii) Coordinated body movements (choreography, technique and synchrony with
music).
(iii) Instrumentation (appropriate instruments, appropriate playing technique, relevant
rhythms and/or melody, and keeping to the beat).
(iv) Appropriate costumes, props and body adornments.
c) Prepare a written synopsis of the folksong outlining:
(i) The community from which the folksong is drawn.
(ii) Gender and age of the performers.
(iii) Occasion during which the folksong is performed.
(iv) Summary of the messages in the folksong.
(vii) Costumes, props and body adornments used in the folksong performance.
d) Take a lead role as a soloist in presenting the folksong.
e) Ensure that the group adheres to the following elements of musicianship in the
performance of the folksong:
(i) Stage presence.
(ii) Vocal energy.
(iii) Artistic passion.
(iv) Focused concentration.
(v) Expressiveness.
Perform folksongs to the audience during the festival for entertainment and display of
culture.
Task 3: Theatre
(i) Brainstorm in groups to generate original and creative ideas inspired by the theme of the
festival.
(ii) Individually develop a story to be presented during the festival.
(iii)Create an outline of the story (with a clear beginning, middle and end) to include character
and setting. The story should be clear coherent with smooth transitions.
The story presentation will focus on
(a)    vocal delivery
(b)    gestures and body language
(c)    facial expressions
Perform stories to the audience during the festival, demonstrating effective storytelling
techniques and engaging the audience.
Turn over
Task 4: Sports
Learners are required to choose a sport of their choice from Handball, Football, Netball,
Volleyball and Rugby. The task requires the learners to work in small teams of between 3 and 5
members to:
a) Explore the game through discussions, watching videos, live matches among other means
and make presentations in a format of choice such as oral, written, pictorial, digital etc.
b) Improvise materials required for the sport.
c) Organise and play the sport while fostering team and sportsmanship spirit.
d) Identify different career opportunities related to the sport.
e) Reflect on personal performance, team dynamics and application of learnt skills.
During the Creative Arts and Sports Festival, some of the selected sports will be presented.

INSTRUCTIONS TO THE AGRICULTURE TEACHER
(a) This paper consists of one performance task on preserving green leafy vegetables
using drying method and is to be completed within a period of two weeks.
(b) The teacher should organise the learners in groups of up to5 members for the task.
(c) The teacher should guide the learners to search for information and write notes on
how to preserve green leafy vegetables using the drying method.
(d) The teacher should guide the groups in choosing one locally available vegetable to
preserve.
(e) The teacher should guide the groups in sourcing for the vegetables they will preserve.
(Examples of vegetables that can be sourced for preservation include spinach, sukuma
wiki, amaranth and any other locally available vegetable).
(f) The teacher should guide the groups in sourcing appropriate tools, equipment and
materials for the task without having to buy new ones. These can be improvised or
sourced from home or school.
(g) The teacher must ensure that learners are dressed appropriately, and they observe
safety during the project.
(h) The teacher should guide the learners to document the process of preserving the
vegetables in an e-portfolio.
(i) The teacher should use the scoring guide provided to assess and score the project task.
NB: 1. The learners should NOT be left on their own at any one time during the task.
2. The learner’s score should be a combination of the individual learner’s score in
criteria 1 and 7, and the group’s score in the other criteria.
@2025 The Kenya National Examinations Council
THEME: FOOD PRSESERVATION FOR FOOD SECURITY
TASK: During the rainy season, the Agriculture Club members witnessed plenty of
green leafy vegetables being taken to the nearby markets. To avoid wastage,
they have planned to prepare and share a documentary with the farmers on how
to preserve the excess vegetables using the drying method.
To accomplish this task, you are required to
1. individually:
a) search for information from parents/guardians/ caregivers, the internet, reference
textbooks and other written materials on how green leafy vegetables can be
preserved using the drying method;
b) write notes on the procedure of drying green leafy vegetables;
c) compile a list of tools, equipment, and materials required when preserving
vegetables using the drying method;
2. work in your group (of up to 5 members) to:
a) discuss and select green leafy vegetable(s) you will preserve;
b) agree on a common procedure you will follow to preserve the green vegetable
selected;
c) assemble the tools, equipment, and materials you will use to preserve the vegetables
using the drying method;
d) preserve the green leafy vegetables selected using the drying method;
e) pack and present the dried vegetables for sale during a school function;
f) observe safety and hygiene while carrying out the task;
g) document the process of preserving the vegetables during the project and keep the
evidence in an e-portfolio;
h) use the e-portfolio to make a presentation on preservation of green leafy vegetables
during a school function.

(i) This project includes activities from all components of the Creative Arts and Sports subject:

(iii) Each task will be assessed using a specific assessment rubric. Learners should have access

reuse materials.

end of the assessment period. Photographs or videos of learners can be taken as they carry
out the tasks and be kept as evidence in their portfolios.
PART I: PERFORMING ARTS                                                         20 Marks
Assessment Task: Group performance of a Kenyan Folksong
With the guidance of the teacher, learners are required to:
1.   Form performance groups of 10 to 15 members
2.   Select an appropriate Kenyan folksong for a performance lasting 2-3 minutes.
3.   Learn the group folksong.
4.   Take a role in the performance as one of the following: soloist, instrumentalist, or
part of the response group.
5.   Perform the folksong for assessment, paying attention to the following aspects:
(i)      Singing with clear tone and voice projection.
(ii)     Clarity of diction and pronunciation of words.
(iii)    Coordinated body movements.
(iv)     Appropriate costumes, props and body adornments.
(v)      An overall performance that entails stage presence, confidence, artistic
passion, focused concentration and expressiveness.

STEPS TO FOLLOW WHEN CREATING THE CRAYON ETCHING ARTWORK:
STEP I: Research on different types of fruits and choose any four (e.g., bananas, grapes,
oranges, mangoes, pineapple, watermelon or others)
STEP II: Draw a still life composition of the four selected fruits arranged in a basket on
drawing paper. Try different layouts. Record the date on all sketches on the day they
are made and keep them safely in your assessment portfolio.
STEP III: Choose the best sketch and colour the fruits using coloured pencils, crayons or paint
to explore suitable colour schemes for the final artwork. Keep the artwork in the
assessment portfolio.
Use the coloured sketch as a reference guide for your crayon etching.
STEP IV: Final artwork on paper measuring 29.7 cm × 30 cm (Size A3)
i. Colour the entire paper using wax crayons in different colours of choice according to
sketch and colouring made at STEP III.
ii. Evenly apply black paint or ink layer over the coloured surface
iii. Carefully etch (scratch) the fruit outlines, textures, and patterns to reveal the fruits,
basket and background details.
iv. Finishing and mounting: Neatly mount the completed artwork, ensure all edges are
straight and tidy.
v. Clearly write your full name and assessment number on the back of the mounted
artwork

THEME: PROCESS FRESH FISH OR DRESS POULTRY CARCASS

PART I: PERFORMING ARTS                                                                     20 Marks
Assessment Task: Group performance of a Kenyan Folk Dance
With the guidance of the teacher, learners are required to:
1.     Make dance performance groups of 12 to 16 members
2.     Select a folk dance from a Kenyan community for a performance lasting 2 – 3 minutes.
3.     Learn and rehearse the songs and dance steps, paying attention to the following aspects:
(i) Authentic singing with clear diction, vocal blend and projection
(ii) Choreography (authentic dance movements, coordinated body movements, pattern
formations and synchrony with music)
(iii) Instrumentation (appropriate instruments, appropriate playing technique, relevant rhythms
and/or melody, and keeping to the beat)
(iv) Appropriate costumes, props, ornaments and body adornments.
4.     Prepare a written synopsis of the folk dance outlining the:
(i) Community from which the folk dance is drawn
(ii) Gender of the performers
(iii) Occasion during which the folk dance is performed
(iv) Message in the folk dance
(v) Role of folk dance in the community
(vi) Ethnic name(s) of instrument(s) accompanying the folk dance.
5.    Take a role in the dance as a soloist, a dancer, an instrumentalist or part of the singing
group in performing the folk dance for assessment.

Marking in Netball
1. Dodging in Netball

Instructions to the Teacher
i.   Identify a safe and appropriate area for performing the assessment tasks.
ii.   Ensure safety of all learners as they perform the task.
iii.   Provide appropriate balls /improvised balls in netball and overarm serve in volleyball. A
volleyball net/improvised net will be required during the serve.
iv.    Overarm serve in volleyball is to be done individually.
v.    Marking and dodging can be organized in trios or in mini games to allow a few learners
participate at a time, enabling more effective assessment.
vi.    Collaborate with other teachers, teacher aides, or authorized personnel to ensure the assessment
runs smoothly and efficiently.
vii.    Provide learners with opportunity for adequate warm up prior to performance of tasks to prepare
their muscles for optimal performance with minimal injuries.
viii.   Give learners opportunity to engage in mini plays, to apply the skills where necessary especially
the marking and dodging
ix.    Score each learner individually in all the tasks.

serve and even in the demonstration of sportsmanship
xi.    Use the scoring guide provided to rate each learner’s performance.
xii.    Ensure that learner(s) with disability are appropriately guided / supported/spotted by
peers/teachers/teacher aides or any other authorised personnel when performing assessment
tasks. They could also be allowed to use their assistive devices when performing the assessment
tasks. Teachers to adhere to the adaptation guidelines for the assessment of learners with special
needs.
Assessing Learner’s ability in marking and dodging in netball
Instructions:
i.   Learners may be organized in groups of three where they could be given roles as follows
ii.   Role 1: Dodger (Attacker) – attempts to dodge and get free so as to receive a pass
iii.   Role 2: Marker (Defender) – tries to mark and prevent the dodger from getting free.
iv.    Role 3: Feeder (with the ball) – stands 3–5 meters away/or at an appropriate distance, ready to pass the
ball if the dodger gets open.
v.   The dodger starts near the marker, facing the feeder.
vi.   On a signal, the dodger tries to use a dodge to get free.
vii.   The marker actively tries to track and block the dodger from receiving the ball
Page |3
viii.     If the dodger gets free, the feeder passes the ball to them.
ix.      Learners may rotate roles every few minutes so that all learners play all roles and get assessed
x.      Where applicable, learners could also be involved in minigames with few attackers and defenders where
teachers assess their skills in a game situation
xi.      Any other arrangement that is appropriate may be adopted by teachers

ASSESSMENT TASK: Montage Picture-Making – “Hilly Landscape at Sunset”
Materials required
i)    Size A4 or A3 drawing paper
ii) Paints or coloured pencils (assorted colours and black)
iii) Old magazines, newspaper, calendars, brochures, fliers
iv) Scissors
v)    Mounting board (old carton box, calendar)
vi) Glue
vii) Old cloth for cleaning hands and workspace
Task description:
A local tourism board is developing a visual campaign to promote beautiful landscapes across the
country. You have been hired to create a montage artwork showing a “Hilly landscape at Sunset”.
Task Instructions:
Individually create a montage using cut-out images from magazines, newspapers, or other printed
sources, focusing on dominance, contrast, and including at least four landscape features. Your final
piece should capture the mood and richness of a sunset scene.
NOTE: All sketches and drawings must be clearly dated at the time they are created and stored in your
assessment portfolio, as they form part of the work to be assessed.
Page |5
To begin the project:
(i) Carry out research on different types of landscapes to help you develop ideas and plan your
composition effectively.
(ii) Sketch the idea of a hilly landscape scene on drawing paper measuring 29.7 cm × 30 cm
(Size A3).
(iii) Paint or colour the drawing to show the colours and forms of hills and sky during sunset.
Pay attention to dominance (what stands out most) and contrast (light vs. dark, warm vs.
cool colours).
(iv) Collect a variety of pictures from old magazines, calendars, fliers, brochures or other
sources but NOT photographs. Look for textures, trees, clouds, rocks and sunset colours
that match the theme of a hilly landscape at sunset.
(v) Neatly cut out the selected pictures and carefully arrange them on the working surface. Use
overlapping to create depth and visual interest. Refer to your sketch as a guide while
placing the images.
(vi) Once you are satisfied with the arrangement, carefully glue each picture in place to
complete the montage.
(vii) Mounting and finishing
o    Ensure your artwork is neat, balanced, and securely glued.
o    Mount your final piece on a clean supporting sheet (such as old cardboard or
carton board).
o    Write your full name and assessment number neatly on the back of the mounted
montage artwork.

Paper 1
Project
May-July 2025
DURATION: 3 months
INSTRUCTIONS TO SCHOOLS
1.   This project paper should be taken in 3 months, during Term II and completed by
31stJuly 2025.
2.   Teachers are provided with scoring guides.
3.   The project will be assessed in parts, where each milestone should be scored, and
a record maintained for each learner.
4.   The project carries a total of 100 marks.
This document consists of 10 printed pages.
©2025 The Kenya National Examinations Council                  Turn over
INTRODUCTION
(i)          This project includes activities from all component disciplines of the Creative Arts and Sports subject:
Performing Arts (Music & Theatre), Sports and Visual Arts.
(ii)         Under the guidance of the teacher, learners are expected to complete all the projects in full. The assessment
scores obtained will contribute to the learner’s final summative assessment.
(iii)        Each task will be assessed using a specific assessment rubric. Learners should have access to the rubric to
ensure their work aligns with the task requirements.
Part 1: Music                        30 marks
The learner is provided with two versions of the music “All Through the Night” in two different keys. The
music in G major is for medium high voice (Soprano and Tenor), while the one in F major is for medium
low voice (Alto and Baritone). Further, an audio recording of the piano accompaniment is provided to
facilitate rehearsal and performance.
Guided by the teacher, the learner is required to:
(i)   Select the song version that is appropriate (as per voice range).
(ii)  Learn, rehearse, and perform the selected song for assessment
(iii) Observe the following aspects during preparation and performance:
a) Note accuracy (rhythm, pitch)
b) Vocal technique (Tone quality, phrasing and breathe control)
c) Diction/Pronunciation of text
d) Performance directions (tempo, dynamics)
e) Compatibility with accompaniment
f) Musicianship
* The music scores are attached after Part 4
Part 2: Theatre                      10 marks
Working in groups of 6 to 8, learners are required to develop, rehearse, and perform a 3-minute story (Narrative)
that addresses a contemporary societal issue.
Task Components
(i)       Composing the Story
• Select a relevant social issue as the theme of the story.
• Develop characters and arrange story milestones in a clear sequence (beginning, middle, and end).
• Write a 3 -minute script, ensuring the story is engaging, well-paced, and with a clear theme.
(ii)      Developing and Refining the Performance
• Rehearse the story, refining voice projection, facial expressions, gestures, and movement.
(iii)     Delivering the Final Performance
• Perform the story with appropriate expression and proper use of voice and body.
• Use appropriate costumes and props.
Part 3: Sports                   30 marks
The task requires the learners to work in groups of between 3 and 5 members. With the assistance of the
teacher/parent/guardian/athletics coach, they are required to:
a) Identify a race classified in the World Athletics Championship (800m, 1500m, 3000m steeplechase with
lower barriers, and 5000m).
b) Explore the race through discussions, watching videos and live performances, and make presentations
in a format of choice such as oral, written, pictorial, digital etc.
c) Discuss and record the rules that govern the race chosen.
d) Identify and improvise materials required for the race.
e) Using the improvised materials, model a mini track and indicate the key features.
f) Participate in the race while fostering team and sportsmanship spirit. (The event may be organised by
school or the community)
g) Identify different career opportunities related to the sport.
h) Reflect on personal performance, team dynamics and application of learnt skills.
i) Maintain a portfolio to show the progress of your work. The portfolio may be physical (hardcopy) or
electronic (soft copy).
Part 4: Visual Arts              30 marks
A newly constructed sports stadium is looking for a beautiful piece of art to enhance its entrance. The goal is to
create a mosaic that represents the energy and motion of sports movements.
Materials required for making the mosaic:
•    Drawing paper
•    Paint or coloured pencils
•    Base for the mosaic (hardboard, cardboard or carton board depending on the type of tesserae)
measuring 29.7 cm × 42 cm (A3 size).
•    Tesserae; coloured paper, banana fibre, eggshells or broken tiles
•    Scissors or suitable cutters (for cutting tesserae where applicable)
•    Glue or adhesive suitable for the materials used
•    Protective covering for the workspace (e.g., old newspapers or carton board or plastic sheet)
•    Cleaning cloth or sponge (for cleaning any excess glue)
Task Description
Design a mosaic for the stadium inspired by the actions of athletes, such as running, jumping, and spinning. The
mosaic should reflect motion using shapes and a suitable colour scheme that captures the energy and movement
of the sporting world.
The mosaic should be made from any one of the following materials: paper, eggshells, banana fibre or broken
tiles.
The complete mosaic should be within an area measuring 29.7 cm × 42 cm (A3 size).
Individually,
(i)       Plan the design: Start by making sketches that relate to sports movement on A4 or A3-sized drawing
papers. Focus on clearly showing the action and movement.
Turn over
(ii)  Choose a colour scheme: Use colours that show action and energy. Paint or colour the sketches, date each
one, and include them in the assessment portfolio as they form part of the final assessment.
(iii) Source the tesserae: Use the chosen colour scheme to find suitable materials for the mosaic pieces.
(iv) Prepare the tesserae: Carefully cut or break the tesserae (mosaic pieces) to ensure clean and precise
pieces for effective arrangement.
(v) Arrange and glue the tesserae on a suitable surface that clearly shows movement and flow. Secure them
with glue, making sure they are firmly attached, with even, neat spacing.
(vi) Finish the mosaic; Ensure that the mosaic is neat with all areas covered and edges tidy with no glue
smears.

INSTRUCTIONS TO LEARNER
(i) This task requires you to carry out research.
(ii) Make several sketches to help you chose the design. Include dates in all the sketches made.
(iii) Keep the sketches in your portfolio.
(iv) Clearly label your portfolio and artwork with your name and assessment number.
(v) Read the rubric before you start and complete the task.
ASSESSMENT TASK
Your school is hosting a Visual Arts exhibition to raise funds for a children’s home. The visual
Arts class has been asked to help by designing and making ornaments for the event.
Guided by your teacher, you are required to make an armlet inspired by culture using different
types of found materials.
a)        Collect and prepare a variety of locally available materials suitable for making an armlet
such as;
• Inedible seeds
• Biro pen tubes
• Natural reeds
• Bamboo sticks
• straws
• Clay beads
• Papier mâché beads
• Paper roll beads
• Cut sticks
• Strings (reused yarns, sisal strings, manilla twine, copper or aluminium wire, nylon
twine etc.)
You may combine any of these materials to make the armlet. Ensure the materials are
appropriate for the project and have unique colour combinations, texture, and shapes.
b)       Make several sketches of the armlet in pencil and chose the best design.
c)       Colour the designs using either paint or colour pencils.
d)       Store all the sketches made in your portfolio.
e)       Measure the circumference of the middle part of your upper arm, to get the size of the
armlet, this can be adjusted depending on how big or small you want the armlet to be.
f)       Using the design chosen, make the armlet using the materials you prepared.
g)       Finish appropriately. Ensure the armlet can be worn.

ASSESSMENT TASK: Armlet made using beadwork technique inspired by culture.
The task requires learners to make an armlet using materials sourced from locally available
materials inspired by culture.

• collect and prepare a variety of locally available materials suitable for making the armlet.

Performing a Kenyan Traditional Group Folk song

in the community,

the community and how to carry out First Aid on a fractured leg or arm,

1.5     in pairs:
(i) write the procedure to follow while carrying out First Aid on a fractured leg or arm,
(ii) identify materials needed to carry out the First Aid,

2. HEALTH EDUCATION GRADE 7 PROJECT
INSTRUCTIONS TO THE TEACHER
(a) This section consists of one performance task: Preparing a health promotional material to:
i) create awareness on a common health concern in the community,
ii) promote individual and community wellness.
b) The teacher to organize learners in groups of up to 6.
c) The teacher to guide learners to keep a journal of the progress of the project.
d) The teacher to guide learners to source for information from multiple sources such as textbooks, resource
persons, parents or guardians, digital devices and the internet and make short notes on:
i) common health concerns in the community
ii) how to prepare health promotional materials.
e) The teacher to guide learners in selecting appropriate resources for carrying out the project.
f) The teacher to encourage learners to share resources where applicable.
g) The teacher to encourage learners to use locally available resources as much as possible as they make the
health promotional materials.
h) The teacher to ensure that learners observe safety measures and precautions while undertaking the project.
i) The teacher to guide learners to display their finished products and explain how the messages promote
individual and community wellness for healthy living.
j) The teacher to guide learners to distribute and share health promotional materials to the school community
k) The teacher to guide learners to reflect on the entire project to establish achievements and areas of
improvement for future projects.
l) The teacher to use the scoring guide provided to assess group performance of the project
m) The teacher to use the group’s score as the individual learner’s score.
n) The teacher to enter the individual learner’s score as project marks in the score sheet provided.

11th August 2023.

PERFORMANCE TASK
Assuming there is a rising health concern in your community that requires members of the public to be made
aware of and have the concern addressed, prepare health promotional materials to:
i) create awareness on the common health concern in the community,
ii) promote individual and community wellness for healthy living.
To perform the task, the learner should:
a) source for information from multiple sources such as textbooks, resource persons, parents or guardians,
digital devices and the internet on:
i) common health concerns in the community
ii) how to prepare health promotional materials.
b) take short notes on common health concerns in the community and how to prepare health promotional
materials.
c) share information collected and discuss common health concerns in the community and how to prepare
health promotional materials.
d) select their preferred health promotional material to make.
e) identify suitable locally available resources they will require to make the selected health promotional
material.
f) make health promotional materials using the locally available resources identified.
g) display the finished product (health promotional material) in the classroom.
h) take a gallery walk to observe their peers’ work, comment and make suggestions for improvement.
i) orally explain how the message contained in the health promotional material creates awareness on a
common health concern in the community to promote wellness of individual and community.
j) distribute and share the health promotional materials with the rest of the school community.
k) keep a journal to show progress of the project.
l) reflect on the entire project to establish achievements and areas of improvement.

INSTRUCTIONS TO THE HEADTEACHER
1.    The school presenting learners for School Based Assessment on Computer Science is required
to provide each group of learners with the following:
(a) Regular learners
(i) A disassembled desktop computer system comprising of various peripheral devices.
(ii) Sufficient work areas to enable the learners carry out the project comfortably.
(iii) Materials for labelling the physical parts of a computer. The materials can be made from
locally available resources.
(b) Learners with physical impairment
(i) A disassembled desktop computer system comprising of various peripheral devices.
(ii) Sufficient work areas to enable the learners carry out the project comfortably.
(iii) Materials for labelling the physical parts of a computer. The materials can be made from
locally available resources and technological interventions.
(iv) Assistive devices where applicable such as:
• Universal communication board, text to speech software or lip-readers for learners with
speech difficulties
• Universal cuffs, wrist/arm braces and arm holders for learners with manipulation
difficulties. The learners can also use alternative functional body parts.
• Adjustable work areas to accommodate learners with varied heights.
(c) Learners with visual impairment
(i) A disassembled desktop computer system comprising of various peripheral devices.
(ii) Sufficient work areas to enable the learners carry out the project comfortably.
(iii) Materials for labelling the physical parts of a computer. The materials can be made from
locally available resources.
(iv) Instructions in large print for those with low visual challenges.

• Magnifying lenses, screen readers and magnifiers for learners with low vision.
• Braille keyboards for blind learners.
